question: From which of the following countries has ‘advisory jurisdiction of the Supreme Court’ been adopted in the Constitution of India?
solution:
The Correct answer is __**Canada**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The concept of **advisory jurisdiction of the Supreme Court** in India has been inspired by the legal system of **Canada.**
 
• Under **Article 143 of the Indian Constitution**, the President of India can seek the opinion of the Supreme Court on matters of **public importance** or cases requiring legal interpretation.
 
• The Supreme Court, in its advisory jurisdiction, provides its opinion, which is termed as **advisory and non-binding**.
 
• The idea of consulting the judiciary for advice ensures a balanced approach to governance and interpretation of law, akin to the practices followed in **Canada.**
 
• Canada has a similar system where the executive can refer matters to the judiciary for opinions, ensuring **judicial review and constitutional clarity.**
 
• This jurisdiction reinforces the role of the Supreme Court as a guardian of the **Constitution** and upholds the principle of **separation of powers** between the legislative, executive, and judiciary.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Cuba**__

 __
 
• **Cuba** follows a socialist form of governance and does not have a system akin to advisory jurisdiction of courts.
 
• The judiciary in Cuba is largely influenced by the **executive and legislative branches**, and there is no independent advisory mechanism for constitutional matters.
 
 
 
• **Germany**__
 __
 
• The judiciary in **Germany** plays a crucial role in constitutional matters through the **Federal Constitutional Court**.
 
• However, Germany does not have a system of advisory jurisdiction like Canada or India. Instead, it focuses on **constitutional review** and adjudication of disputes.
 
 
 
• **Portugal**__
 
 
• **Portugal** operates under a civil law system and does not follow the concept of advisory jurisdiction.
 
• Its judiciary ensures compliance with constitutional provisions but does not have a dedicated mechanism for offering advisory opinions to the executive.
